Getting Started

OpenFlows is an autonomous AI development team that runs 24/7 on your GitHub repository. Five agents - NEXUS, FORGE, SENTINEL, VESSEL, and LORE - collaborate to take issues all the way to merged, documented pull requests without human intervention.

What you will accomplish

By the end of this guide you will have OpenFlows installed, configured, and running against a real GitHub repository, turning open issues into reviewed, merged PRs.

1. Prerequisites

RequirementDetailsInstall
Node.js 18+Required for the GitHub MCP server and npm installhttps://nodejs.org
Code agent CLIClaude Code or Codex CLI - the hands FORGE uses to write filesnpm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
or
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/codex-cli
GitHub PATsOne per agent with repo + workflow scopeshttps://github.com/settings/tokens
LLM API keyAnthropic, OpenAI, or FireworksProvider dashboard
Rust 1.70+Only needed if building from sourcehttps://rustup.rs

Claude Code vs Codex CLI

Both are Anthropic-powered code agents. Claude Code is the original CLI; Codex CLI is a newer lightweight interface. Set DEFAULT_CLI=codex or DEFAULT_CLI=claude in your environment to choose. FORGE will invoke whichever you select.

2. Install OpenFlows

Choose the method that fits your setup. All methods install the same binaries: openflows, openflows-setup, openflows-dashboard, and openflows-doctor.

Fastest on any platform with Node.js already installed.

npm install -g @the-agenticflow/openflows openflows --version

Downloads the correct pre-built binary for your OS and architecture, installs to ~/.local/bin.

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-AgenticFlow/OpenFlows/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

For Rust developers who prefer cargo.

cargo install openflows openflows --version

Run in a container. Mounts your config directory for persistence.

docker run -it --rm \ -v "$HOME/.openflows:/home/openflows/.openflows" \ -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_key \ -e GITHUB_REPOSITORY=owner/repo \ ghcr.io/the-agenticflow/openflows:latest

See the Installation Guide for Homebrew, source builds, and Compose setups with Redis and LiteLLM.

3. Configure Your Environment

OpenFlows needs two files: a .env with tokens and keys, and a registry.json that maps each agent to its LLM model. You can generate both with the interactive wizard, or write them manually.

The TUI wizard asks for your repository, tokens, and preferred CLI, then writes .env and registry.json automatically.

openflows-setup

It will walk you through:

  1. Target GitHub repository
  2. Per-agent GitHub tokens
  3. LLM provider and API keys
  4. Preferred code agent (Claude Code or Codex CLI)
  5. Model registry for each agent

Copy the template below into a .env file in your working directory. Every variable is documented inline.

# ── Core ──────────────────────────────────────── # The repository the team will work on GITHUB_REPOSITORY=your-org/your-repo # Code agent: "claude" for Claude Code, "codex" for Codex CLI DEFAULT_CLI=codex # The command OpenFlows uses to invoke the GitHub MCP server. # Example for the official MCP: npx -y @anthropic-ai/github-mcp-server GITHUB_MCP_CMD=npx -y @anthropic-ai/github-mcp-server # ── Per-Agent GitHub Tokens ───────────────────── # Each agent gets its own PAT so actions are auditable per identity. # Create tokens at https://github.com/settings/tokens with scopes: # repo, workflow, read:org (for NEXUS), delete_repo (for VESSEL cleanup) AGENT_NEXUS_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_nexus_token_here AGENT_FORGE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_forge_token_here AGENT_SENTINEL_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_sentinel_token_here AGENT_VESSEL_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_vessel_token_here # ── LLM API Keys ──────────────────────────────── # Provide at least one key matching the models declared in registry.json. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api-key-here OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-openai-api-key-here # FIREWORKS_API_KEY=your_fireworks_key_here # optional # ── Debug / Logging ───────────────────────────── RUST_LOG=info,agent_team=debug,pocketflow_core=debug

Token scopes

Each agent token needs repo and workflow scopes. NEXUS benefits from read:org for team assignment logic, and VESSEL may need delete_repo if you enable branch cleanup. Never reuse the same token across agents - per-agent tokens are what make actions auditable.

3.1 Model Registry (registry.json)

The registry tells each agent which LLM to use. You can mix providers - FORGE on Claude Sonnet, SENTINEL on Gemini, NEXUS on GPT-4o. This multi-model setup creates natural adversarial review.

json
{
  "agents": {
    "nexus":    { "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514" },
    "forge":    { "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514" },
    "sentinel": { "provider": "openai",    "model": "gpt-4.1" },
    "vessel":   { "provider": "openai",    "model": "gpt-4o" },
    "lore":     { "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-haiku-4-20250514" }
  }
}

The TUI wizard generates this for you. For manual setup, place registry.json next to your .env file. Hot-reloaded on every NEXUS poll - no restart required.

4. Verify Installation

Run the built-in doctor to check every dependency before starting the team.

bash
openflows-doctor

Expected output:

bash
$ openflows-doctor
  Rust toolchain:   1.88.0
  Node.js:          v20.11.0
  Code agent CLI:   codex (found in PATH)
  Git:              2.44.0
  GitHub tokens:    4/4 present
  LLM API keys:     ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set
  GITHUB_REPOSITORY: owner/repo
  registry.json:    valid

Missing something?

The doctor prints exactly which token or binary is missing and a link to where to get it. Fix it, re-run, and proceed.

5. Run the Autonomous Team

Two terminals: one runs the orchestration engine, the other shows real-time worker status.

bash
# Terminal 1 - start the engine
openflows

# Terminal 2 - real-time dashboard
openflows-dashboard

What happens when you start openflows:

  1. NEXUS polls GitHub for open issues and worker state
  2. Idle issues are assigned to FORGE workers with unique ticket IDs
  3. Each FORGE creates a Git worktree, writes PLAN.md, and implements segment by segment
  4. SENTINEL reviews every segment against 5 criteria before approving
  5. VESSEL handles CI status, conflicts, and squash-merges approved PRs
  6. LORE writes ADRs and updates CHANGELOG.md after each merge

6. What the Logs Look Like

From open issue to merged PR in approximately 16 minutes. No human intervention.

bash
INFO  Starting REAL End-to-End Orchestration
INFO  Loaded 6 worker slots: [nexus, forge-1, forge-2, sentinel, vessel, lore]
INFO  Found 3 open issues
INFO  Assigning issue #1 to forge-1  ->  T-001
INFO  Worktree created: forge-1/T-001
INFO  Spawning code agent for forge-1
INFO  PLAN.md written - spawning SENTINEL for review
INFO  Contract AGREED - implementation starting
INFO  Worker forge-1 completed - PR opened: #1
INFO  CI status: success for PR #1
INFO  PR #1 merged successfully
INFO  LORE: ADR-001 written and committed

Next Steps

Now that the team is running:

  • Read the Agent Setup guide to tune model routing, worker slots, and per-agent prompts
  • Study Agent Roles to understand each agent's contract and recovery behavior
  • Check FAQ for common troubleshooting (rate limits, token scopes, CI timeouts)

Need help?

If the doctor reports a missing dependency or NEXUS fails to assign tickets, start with theFAQ or open a discussion onGitHub Discussions.
